newsitem.title: FRANCE: Defence minister foresees NATO, WEU membership.
newsitem.headline: Defence minister foresees NATO, WEU membership.

text.p: Austria's Defence Minister said on Tuesday he believed his country would become a member of both NATO and the Western European Union (WEU) to enable it to play a full role in international affairs.

"It is my belief that it is only a matter of time until we come to full membership, otherwise Austria loses all possibility of influencing major decisions," Werner Fasslabend told reporters in the margins of a WEU meeting in Paris.
Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima has said he will hold a referendum on whether the country, which adopted neutrality in 1955, should join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

Fasslabend, making clear he was referring to both NATO and WEU membership, said he thought his country would review its position after NATO invites new members from former communist Europe to join the alliance next July.
"An effective security policy without full participation in the WEU and NATO is not possible," he added.
Austria, which joined the European Union some two years ago, enjoys only observer status at the WEU, the EU's designated defence wing.
"From the point of view of Austria, that is not satisfactory," Fasslabend said.
If as expected, NATO invites Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic to join the alliance, Austria will be virtually surrounded by NATO members.
"NATO has evolved into a different organisation and the reason for Austria's neutrality has disappeared," said one NATO official.
He added he believed other "neutrals" such as Sweden and Finland would also soon change their position and apply to join the alliance.
